summary: Summit site of a 1934 L-4 cab, dated to the 1960s and described as removed, abandoned or destroyed; a half-mile trail climbs to the summit.

facts.status_note: The L-4 cab is gone. Sources date its end to the 1960s but differ on whether it was removed, abandoned or destroyed.

access.note: Forest Service page says Trail 132 is open to hikers and horses, but the same page carries a Trail Temporarily Closed banner.

visit.trail_note: Trail 132A, about 0.5 miles, climbs from Trail 132 to the summit. Trail 132 ends on Road 58 at the Observation Peak Trailhead. Willhite gives 2.5 miles from the north trailhead.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Service says abandoned in the 1960s; register says removed in the 1960s; firelookout.com and Willhite say destroyed in the 1960s. The decade agrees and the verb does not. The story reports the disagreement rather than choosing one.

Register and Forest Service give 1934 for the L-4 cab. Willhite says the earlier D-6 cupola appears only in the lookout inventory, and a 1934 panoramic survey skipped the peak, so the earlier cabin is uncertain. Willhite wonders whether a cupola cabin stood here before 1934, but thinks a dismantled cupola may be on the ground in the 1937 panorama.

notes_for_editor: No source describes what remains on the summit today. The Forest Service trail page shows a Trail Temporarily Closed banner beside the open-to-hikers line, so check current trail status before publishing the access line. The Oregonian items were read through Kemnow and Willhite quotations, not the newspapers. Record coordinates, elevation and the 2012 FFLOS registration match the register. Record kind ground is consistent with the Forest Association list.
